subject: research/sensing-recon
professional: a multi-view geometry / structure-from-motion researcher (the Hartley-Zisserman, COLMAP kind); first checks: do the triangulation errors match first-order covariance propagation, is each perturbation (pixel, pose, baseline) the thing its label says, is the error metric a true distance, and is the view-count result new against the photogrammetry and MVS-benchmark literature

evidence.correctness: Reran `python3 experiments/run.py` (python 3.13, numpy 2.5.3) in a scratch copy: 14 s, output identical to the committed results.txt (only diff is print's trailing newline). Independent recomputation in /tmp/claude-0/round94-sensing/indep.py: my own look-at cameras, own visibility rule, midpoint (least-squares ray) triangulation instead of DLT, and a first-order covariance prediction (Hartley and Zisserman 2004, ch. 5, backward propagation, Cov = sigma^2 (J^T J)^-1, E|g.dX| = sqrt(2/pi) sqrt(g^T Cov g)). Completeness 0.133 / 0.588 / 0.894 / 1.000 at 4/6/8/12 views (README 0.133, 0.588, 0.894, 1.000); 12 views mean error 0.0014 at 0.5 px, 0.0028 at 1 px, 0.0112 at 4 px, 48 views 0.0007, and the first-order prediction 0.0014 / 0.0028 / 0.0111 / 0.0007: all within 0.0001 of results.txt. The numbers are right for what the code computes. Two outputs measure something other than their label: the 'pose error' sweep D (rotation pre-multiplied with t kept) swings each camera about the object centre, and the error metric is the radial offset, which exceeds the Euclidean distance by about 8% (0.0028 vs 0.0026 at 1 px, 0.0112 vs 0.0103 at 4 px). Those are claims defects (below), so correctness stays 3.
evidence.completeness: Everything the README lists runs: 11 tests pass (0.88 s), run.py reproduces results.txt, figure.py reads section A. Sweeps A-E all present. The track brief's Chamfer-against-scan, SfM, MVS and splats are declared out of scope, not claimed. Stale leftovers: pyproject description and module docstring still said 'Chamfer'; run.py section E header said '2..48' while the loop starts at 3. Live page https://marisstella.app/research/sensing-recon/ could not be loaded (curl status 000 through the proxy); the homepage summary in research/_homepage/projects.json was checked instead.
evidence.verification: `cd research/sensing-recon && PYTHONPATH=src python3.13 -m pytest -q tests`: 11 passed in 0.88 s. Seven mutants with platform/ci/quality_mutate.py on the original code: only one caught (ray-angle min -> max). Survived: MIN_COS 0.25 -> 0.40, min_angle_deg 2.0 -> 0.0, elevation alternation removed, pixel noise doubled, pose rotation K doubled, surface_error x1.5. The tests check signs and orderings (more views > fewer, noise raises error) and pin no magnitude, so every headline number in the README could change by a factor without a red test. After the fix (7 new tests) all seven corresponding mutants are caught; the score records the state before the fix.
evidence.craft: Read src/sensing_recon/recon.py (164 lines), __init__.py, tests/test_recon.py, experiments/run.py, figure.py. Small, readable, numpy only, deterministic seeds. Defects: the pose perturbation (recon.py:153-158) pre-multiplies R and keeps t, so the camera centre -R^T t moves on a sphere around the origin; this is a classic pose-parameterisation slip and it changes the meaning of sweep D. The rotation I + K + K^2/2 is orthogonal only to second order. DLT is run on raw pixel coordinates with no Hartley normalisation (harmless here: my midpoint triangulation agrees to 1e-4). Per-point Python loop in triangulate_all. Stale 'Chamfer' in the module docstring and pyproject.
evidence.claims: Backed (recomputed): the completeness knee 0/6.6/13.3/58.8/89.4/100%, the 0.0028 radii per px slope, error flat in view count and falling to 0.0007 at 48, section E's 12 views. Not backed or wrong: (1) 'A 1 deg pose error therefore does the damage of roughly 2 px' (README.md:30, repeated in research/_homepage/projects.json:3905): with t kept the camera moves along the orbit and the object stays centred; a true 1 deg orientation error (rotation about the camera centre) gives mean error 0.0357, not 0.0064, i.e. about 13 px of noise (/tmp/claude-0/round94-sensing/pose.py, now sweep D2 in results.txt); the Limitations line 'Pose error is a random rotation only (no position error)' is the reverse of what the code does. (2) The 2 deg-span survivors 'pass the 2 deg ray test by chance of geometry' (README.md:29): they are the points the +30 and -30 deg cameras both see, about 60 deg apart; the span sweep is confounded by the alternating elevation. (3) Error called 'the distance ... to the exact surface': it is the radial offset, about 8% larger. Limitations otherwise candid.
evidence.fitness: Job: a researcher wants a reusable baseline for 'how many views, how much noise, how much pose error' before running real SfM. They get a small, reproducible triangulation harness whose noise slope and view knee check out against first-order theory. Nearest prior work: Hartley and Zisserman 2004 ch. 5 and 12 (first-order triangulation covariance; error linear in sigma and shrinking roughly with 1/sqrt(views) is textbook), Hartley and Sturm 1997 'Triangulation' (CVIU) for DLT vs optimal triangulation, Seitz et al. 2006 (Middlebury MVS) and Knapitsch et al. 2017 (Tanks and Temples) for view-count/accuracy on real objects, and Schonberger and Frahm 2016 (cited). Nothing here is new beyond a worked example: the completeness knee is a property of the chosen rig (cos 0.25 visibility, +/-30 deg alternation, 2 deg ray rule), which the README admits, and the one non-obvious result (pose vs pixel trade-off) was mislabelled. Sound as a teaching harness; not yet something a PhD-level programme would build a paper on.
evidence.domain: Against standard practice in multi-view geometry: DLT triangulation is the textbook linear method (fine, though unnormalised and not the optimal/midpoint method Hartley-Sturm compare); the ray-angle gate is the COLMAP practice (min triangulation angle), good. Departures a reviewer would flag first: pose error modelled as a rotation about the world origin and labelled orientation error; the 'baseline' sweep varies azimuth span while elevation alternation fixes a 60 deg baseline between neighbours; error metric is a radial offset, not point-to-surface distance; no comparison to the analytic covariance the field uses as the reference (I supplied one and it agrees); no bundle adjustment, which is what real pipelines use to absorb pose error.

defects.what: Sweep D's 'pose error' pre-multiplies each camera rotation and keeps t, which rotates the camera about the object centre (centre moves ~4 radii x angle, object stays centred, ~3 px image shift per deg). The README reads it as an orientation error and concludes a 1 deg pose error costs about 2 px of noise; a true 1 deg orientation error gives mean error 0.0357 vs 0.0064, about 13 px. Limitations said 'rotation only (no position error)', the reverse. Fixed in the subject: perturb_rotation() with about_centre, new sweep D2, README corrected, tests added.

Baseline sweep confounded by the alternating +/-30 deg elevation: neighbouring cameras are always ~60 deg apart, only same-elevation pairs are narrow, and the 2 deg-span survivors are the wide-baseline cross-elevation points, not 'chance of geometry'. Fixed in README wording; the sweep itself still does not isolate a narrow rig.

Tests pin no magnitudes: 6 of 7 seeded mutants (visibility cosine, ray-angle rule, elevation pattern, noise scale x2, pose rotation x2, error metric x1.5) survived. Fixed: 7 new tests, all 7 mutants now caught.

Error metric described as the distance to the exact surface; it is the radial offset |r - R(d)|, about 8% larger than the Euclidean distance here. Fixed in README and docstring, with a test bounding the ratio.
Stale text: pyproject description and module docstring still said 'Chamfer' after Chamfer was dropped; run.py section E header said '2..48' though the loop starts at 3. Fixed.

The homepage summary still says 'a 1° pose error does the damage of about 2 px'; outside the subject directory, not fixed in this audit. Should say a 1 deg orientation error costs about 13 px (sweep D2).

Small-rotation update I + K + K^2/2 is not exactly orthogonal (fixed: Rodrigues, results unchanged to 4 dp); DLT runs on unnormalised pixel coordinates with no Hartley normalisation (not fixed; midpoint triangulation agrees to 1e-4 here, so harmless at this scale).

No novelty positioning: the noise slope and view averaging are exactly the first-order textbook prediction (HZ ch. 5), which the README does not compare against, and the completeness knee is a property of chosen rig constants; no real-data or SfM comparison (Seitz et al. 2006, Knapitsch et al. 2017 not cited). Not fixed (ROADMAP-sized).

verdict: A small, clean, reproducible triangulation harness whose core numbers are right: I reran the experiment (identical) and recomputed completeness and the 0.0028 radii/px slope with my own cameras, a midpoint triangulator and first-order covariance propagation, all to within 0.0001. It misses the bar on claims and verification. The headline 'a 1 deg pose error costs about 2 px' is wrong: the code keeps t when rotating, which moves the camera around the object rather than turning it, and a true 1 deg orientation error costs about 13 px (0.0357 vs 0.0064). The baseline sweep is confounded by the alternating elevation, the error 'distance' is a radial offset 8% larger, and 6 of 7 seeded mutants survived because the tests pin no magnitudes. Fixed in the subject directory (uncommitted, no PR yet): perturb_rotation with an about-centre option and new sweep D2, Rodrigues rotation, corrected README and docstrings, 7 new tests killing all 7 mutants (18 pass). Still open: the homepage summary repeats the 2 px claim, and the project has no novelty beyond the textbook first-order result.
